issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a subroutine named set_pixel that performs the pixel write (called from main). The template provides an empty set_pixel stub, but the solution defines a subroutine named write_pixel (with the intended implementation) while main still calls set_pixel. This name/signature mismatch means the provided solution is structurally inconsistent with the template and will fail to assemble/link (undefined label), and students will be confused which symbol to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the subroutine name consistent: either rename the solution's write_pixel to set_pixel (so it replaces the template stub), or change main to call write_pixel. Ensure the implemented subroutine matches the specification (parameters/register conventions) described in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a subroutine named 'set_pixel', but the solution implementation defines a function named 'write_pixel' while the main code still calls 'set_pixel'. This name mismatch (set_pixel vs write_pixel) breaks the conceptual mapping between the required subroutine in the exercise and the provided solution code and will confuse students trying to locate or reuse the expected routine.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the subroutine across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'write_pixel' function to 'set_pixel' (or update the call sites to call 'write_pixel') so the solution, template, and problem statement all reference the same subroutine name.
